General Appearance:
A slight High Elf with an earthy complexion, quiet footing, and restless
energy visible in her hands and eyes. Her appearance is natural and
unadorned, but there is something electrically vivid about her attention.

She wears leather armor beneath an acolyte robe adapted for travel. Her

her combined work as religious performer, oral historian, and traveler.

FEATURES AND ABILITIES

PERSONALITY TRAITS

Bard 1 is highly charismatic and clever enough to make simple situations
complicated.

In danger, her instincts are excellent. Her battle songs are lively, direct,
well timed, and exactly suited to keeping frightened people moving. When she
uses Bardic Inspiration in a crisis, the performance feels immediate and
practical rather than scholarly.

Outside battle, she is an ethnographer of endangered vocal traditions. She
collects songs, chants, work rhythms, laments, ceremonial responses, and oral
histories from cultures whose music is being displaced, forgotten, or absorbed
into larger societies.

Her collection includes far-northern sea chants, mountain antiphonies, songs
from the dry interior, call-and-response traditions from the deep plains,
river-delta work music, court ballads from distant eastern kingdoms, island
percussion chants, pastoral throat-singing, and fragmentary songs attributed
to peoples from a lost continent several continents away.

This makes her tavern performances unpredictable. An audience expecting a
familiar drinking song or romantic ballad may instead receive a funeral chant
from an isolated plateau community or a rowing cadence from a vanished coastal
people.

When she performs well, her Charisma and respect for the material allow the
song to reach people even when it is unfamiliar. The audience may not
understand the original context, but the emotion survives the translation.

When she performs poorly, the result can feel baffling, overly academic, or
completely unsuited to the room. Listeners may wonder why they are hearing an
obscure ritual clicking song when they ordered another round and wanted
something cheerful.

Of the two former acolytes, Bard 1 is the more active proselytizer for the
Common Table. In every new settlement, she looks for beggars, displaced
families, isolated travelers, hungry children, injured laborers, and people
being ignored by local authority.

She will interrupt an urgent mission to help such people, even when the rest
of the group insists that a larger threat must come first. She does not accept
that saving the world excuses walking past the person suffering directly in
front of her.

Bard 1 deeply distrusts people from large cities. She assumes that dense urban
life rewards indifference, deception, status-seeking, and the habit of treating
strangers as disposable. A city resident must prove trustworthy before she
grants them the benefit of the doubt.

Her distrust is broad and unfair. It is a prejudice, not an accurate rule about
urban people.

IDEALS

Faith.

Bard 1 trusts that the principles of the Common Table are larger and more
enduring than any official who misuses them. Hospitality, the preservation of
names, mutual aid, and safe passage remain sacred even when a religious
institution fails to practice them.

Her faith is not confidence that every mystery will be explained. It is a
decision to continue carrying names, testimony, food, warning, and hope when
the people entrusted with those duties become corrupt.

Source Roll: Acolyte Ideal d6 result 5.

BONDS

Bard 1 intends to take revenge on the corrupt religious hierarchy that helped
expose the House of Shared Bread and the refuge network connected to it.

Her revenge is not defined as assassination or indiscriminate destruction.
She wants the responsible officials identified publicly, stripped of authority,
deprived of the records and resources they controlled, and forced to hear the
names of every person harmed by their decisions.

She suspects that someone within the Common Table supplied the false pilgrims
with authentic phrases, seals, and sanctuary customs.

Source Roll: Acolyte Bond d6 result 2.

FLAWS

Bard 1 places too much trust in people who hold recognized authority within
her religious tradition.

A title, official robe, seal, or formal appointment carries more weight with
her than it should. Even after the attack, her first instinct is to distinguish
one corrupt official from the institution rather than question whether the
institution itself enabled the harm.

This flaw is particularly dangerous because her Bond directs her against a
hierarchy she still instinctively respects.

Source Roll: Acolyte Flaw d6 result 2.

ALLIES AND ORGANIZATIONS

Name or Group: The Common Table
Relationship or Connection:
Bard 1's religious tradition and active missionary cause

Notes:
The Common Table operates kitchens, guest halls, shrines, road refuges, and
networks for food, letters, names, routes, and safe passage.

Bard 1 remains committed to its principles while investigating corruption in
its upper administration. She also actively carries those principles into new
places by seeking out people excluded from ordinary aid and helping them
directly.

Name or Group: The House of Shared Bread
Relationship or Connection:
Former sanctuary and spiritual home

False pilgrims attacked the sanctuary and stole the Wayfarer Ledger after
someone silenced its alarm bell.

Name or Group: The Chorus of Returning Names
Relationship or Connection:
Loose network of singers, reciters, messengers, mourners, and oral historians

Notes:
The Chorus preserves testimony independently of official archives. Members
memorize names, routes, losses, debts, and acts of aid so that destroying one
ledger cannot erase an event.

The Chorus is not formally controlled by the Common Table hierarchy. Some
members believe official centralization of refuge records directly caused the
attack on the House of Shared Bread.

Supporting Organization Roll: d20 result 18.

Name or Group: Senior Cantor Maelis Thorn
Relationship or Connection:
Former teacher, institutional sponsor, and unresolved suspect

Notes:
Maelis trained Bard 1 in oral registers, ceremonial performance, and the
discipline of repeating a name exactly as given.

Maelis personally vouched for the distant charitable order whose supposed
pilgrims later attacked the sanctuary. Bard 1 does not know whether Maelis was
deceived, coerced, careless, or complicit.

Bard 1's instinctive respect for Maelis's office makes the question harder to
investigate honestly.

Supporting Relationship Roll: d20 result 3.

CHARACTER NOTES, GOALS, FEARS, AND RELATIONSHIPS

Goals:

Bard 1 wants to identify the official or officials who supplied the false
pilgrims with authentic seals, phrases, and sanctuary customs.

She wants to find Senior Cantor Maelis Thorn and determine whether her former
teacher was deceived or participated knowingly.

She also wants to build the Many-Mouth Register, a distributed oral record in
which no single captured courier, stolen ledger, destroyed shrine, or corrupt
administrator can expose or erase the entire refuge network.

Supporting Goal Roll: d20 result 8.

Fears:

Bard 1 fears that one of her own public recitations helped the attackers.

Before the assault, she performed a formal journey litany at a regional
gathering. The litany contained names, repeated phrases, route metaphors, and
traditional responses used by legitimate travelers.

She does not know whether someone extracted practical information from the
performance or whether that fear is guilt searching for a shape.

More deeply, she fears discovering that Maelis knowingly used her voice to
authenticate a betrayal.

Supporting Fear Roll: d20 result 5.

Habits or Mannerisms:

She records songs phonetically before translating them, then writes separate
notes for rhythm, breathing, gesture, social setting, and who is permitted to
perform them.

She becomes irritated when another performer “improves” a traditional song by
making it smoother, more fashionable, or easier for outsiders to enjoy.

Before a battle, she instinctively chooses simple, forceful music with a clear
pulse. In a tavern, she is much more likely to select something historically
important and socially baffling.

After a successful unusual performance, she explains the song's origin only
if asked. After an unsuccessful one, she is prone to explaining it at length
to an audience that has already stopped listening.

Upon entering a new settlement, she scans alleys, market edges, shrine steps,
work yards, and roadside shelters for people who have been excluded from the
community's ordinary support.

She carries small portions of food separately so they can be given away
without opening the group's entire ration supply. This does not create extra
rations or override the recorded inventory.

When someone says, “We do not have time to help everyone,” she usually replies
with some version of, “We have time to help this one.”

She asks where a stranger is from early in conversation. Mention of a major
city makes her noticeably more guarded, skeptical, and formal.

She tends to interpret urban polish, fashionable clothing, official confidence,
and quick salesmanship as warning signs until shown otherwise.

Important Relationships:

Senior Cantor Maelis Thorn:
Former teacher whose possible connection to the false pilgrims threatens
Bard 1's faith in religious authority.

The House of Shared Bread:
Former home and center of the attack that began the pair's journey.

The Chorus of Returning Names:
Independent oral-history network that may offer a safer future for sanctuary
records.

The Common Table:
Her faith tradition, whose principles she still serves while opposing parts
of its hierarchy.

Other Character Notes:

Her ethnographic work is intended to preserve endangered vocal traditions
respectfully. She records where a song comes from, who may perform it, what
occasion it belongs to, and what should not be altered merely to please an
outside audience.

Her distrust of large-city residents is a character flaw and prejudice. It
grants no automatic Insight, social advantage, immunity to deception, or
special knowledge of urban people.

Her charitable interventions use her actual equipment, money, spell slots,
time, and judgment. They do not create unlimited food, shelter, healing, or
funds.

Her bagpipes are both a musical instrument and her normal Bard spellcasting
focus.

Her proficiency with lute and pan flute does not mean those instruments are
present in her starting equipment.

The bag of forty-seven teeth is a mundane trinket. The teeth have not been
identified by creature or origin. One is rotten. The AI Game Master may use
the bag as a future mystery, but it grants no automatic magical or forensic
information.

The Wayfarer Ledger, Maelis Thorn, corruption within the Common Table, the
Many-Mouth Register, and Bard 1's potentially compromised recital are future
AI Game Master story hooks.

Formative Event Roll: d20 result 15.
The formative event is the regional journey litany that may have revealed
information later used against the sanctuary.


BACKSTORY

Bard 1 was born in a High Elf community whose long memory was maintained less
through monuments than through repeated names, seasonal songs, and carefully
preserved accounts of who traveled where and why.

She entered the Common Table after hearing one of its traveling cantors recite
the names of people who had vanished during a winter migration. The list did
not transform them into heroes. It simply refused to let absence become
erasure.

At the House of Shared Bread, Bard 1 became a Wayfarer Cantor.

She announced meals, welcomed travelers, taught children road songs, performed
at memorials, copied letters, carried warnings between guest houses, and
maintained oral versions of important records.

Another acolyte served at the same sanctuary, maintaining stores, written
ledgers, ritual texts, and practical guest records. Bard 1 preserved names,
journeys, and testimony in forms that could survive the loss of paper.

Senior Cantor Maelis Thorn trained and sponsored her. Maelis taught that a
cantor's first obligation was exactness: never improve a person's name for
rhythm, never replace an unfamiliar place with a familiar one, and never turn
someone's suffering into a prettier story.

Bard 1 trusted her.

At a regional gathering, Bard 1 performed a formal journey litany before
officials, pilgrims, traders, and representatives of distant charitable
orders. Maelis approved the program and vouched for several visiting guests.

Weeks later, travelers wearing the symbols of one of those orders arrived at
the House of Shared Bread during bad weather. A fellow acolyte argued that
they should be admitted. Bard 1 recognized the phrases and ceremonial
responses they used. The House opened its doors.

The visitors were not pilgrims.

They silenced the alarm bell, wounded Mother Orra Vale, searched the archive,
and stole the Wayfarer Ledger. Bard 1 used magic, voice, and remembered
passages through the sanctuary to help move survivors out.

Afterward, she found details that troubled her. The attackers had used
authentic formulas rarely known outside trained staff. One had repeated a
line from her regional journey litany with the same unusual phrasing she had
used in performance.

Bard 1 left to follow the stolen ledger. It remains missing, her former
teacher's role remains unresolved, and she fears that her own performance may
have helped teach the attackers how to enter.


OPTIONAL BACKSTORY

This is optional story material only. It does not establish current party membership, leadership, or party role.

Bard 1 and Warlock 1 served together at the House of Shared Bread. After the sanctuary was attacked and the Wayfarer Ledger stolen, they left together to follow it. Their search led toward an illegal trapping and labor camp. Druid 1 had independently tracked damaged land, poisoned water, and abnormal animal movement to the same location. Barbarian 1 entered by another route seeking contracts, keys, and payroll records. When the camp's alarms sounded, the four investigations collided. Druid 1 found a safe route through the surrounding wetland, Barbarian 1 opened a barred service gate, and Warlock 1 and Bard 1 used magic, memory, and coordination to move captives through the confusion. The four escaped together and continued traveling as the Wild party.

Bard Spellcasting: Charisma-based; bagpipes or another musical instrument can serve as focus.
High Elf Lineage: knows Message using Charisma and can replace it with a Wizard cantrip after a Long Rest.
Fey Ancestry: Advantage on saves to avoid or end Charmed. SRD rules: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Charmed condition.
Keen Senses: Perception proficiency. SRD rules: You have proficiency in the Insight, Perception, or Survival skill.

Trance: does not need sleep, magic cannot put her to sleep, and she may Long Rest in 4 conscious trancelike hours. SRD rules: You don’t need to sleep, and magic can’t put you to sleep. You can finish a Long Rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a trancelike meditation, during which you retain consciousness.

Magic Initiate (Cleric): Guidance, Light, and Bless; Charisma casting; Bless is always prepared and free once per Long Rest. SRD rules: Origin Feat. You gain the following benefits. Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat’s spells (choose when you select this feat). Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat’s cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list. Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different spell list each time.
Acolyte background: Insight, Religion, and Calligrapher's Supplies proficiencies.
Tool proficiencies: Bagpipes, Calligrapher's supplies, Lute, Pan flute.

Spellcasting — You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Bard spells, which appear in the Bard spell list later in the class’s description. Cantrips. You know two cantrips of your choice from the Bard spell list. Dancing Lights and Vicious Mockery are recommended. Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list. When you reach Bard levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Bard Features table. Spell Slots. The Bard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest. Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Bard spell list. Charm Person, Color Spray, Dissonant Whispers, and Healing Word are recommended. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Bard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Bard spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you’re a level 3 Bard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination. If another Bard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Bard spells for you. Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Bard spell for which you have spell slots. Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Bard spells. Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus for your Bard spells.

story_facts.fact: Bard 1 is a Wayfarer Cantor of the Common Table, devoted to hospitality, mutual aid, safe passage, and preserving names so vulnerable people are not erased.
She formerly served at the House of Shared Bread, where she preserved names, journeys, warnings, local history, and testimony through recitation and music.
False pilgrims attacked the House of Shared Bread, wounded Mother Orra Vale, silenced its alarm bell, and stole the Wayfarer Ledger.
The attackers used authentic sanctuary formulas and one repeated unusual wording from Bard 1's journey litany; she fears her public recital helped enable the assault.
Senior Cantor Maelis Thorn, Bard 1's former teacher and sponsor, vouched for the supposed charitable order; Bard 1 does not know whether Maelis was deceived, coerced, careless, or complicit.
Bard 1 seeks the stolen Wayfarer Ledger, evidence of institutional corruption, and the truth of Maelis Thorn's role.
She intends to create the Many-Mouth Register, a distributed oral record that cannot be erased through one stolen ledger, courier, shrine, or administrator.
The Chorus of Returning Names is an independent network of singers, reciters, messengers, mourners, and oral historians preserving names, routes, losses, debts, and acts of aid.
She is an ethnographer of endangered vocal traditions and tries to preserve songs respectfully, including restrictions on who may perform them and what should not be altered.
Her broad distrust of large-city residents is explicitly a prejudice and grants no mechanical insight, advantage, or special knowledge.
The bag of forty-seven teeth is mundane, unidentified, and grants no automatic magical, tracking, forensic, or creature-identification benefit.

In danger, uses lively, direct, practical battle songs to keep frightened people moving.
Outside combat, collects endangered songs, chants, work rhythms, laments, ceremonial responses, and oral histories.
Tavern performances can be historically important but socially baffling; after a poor performance she tends to overexplain it.
Actively seeks excluded, hungry, displaced, injured, or ignored people in every settlement and may interrupt urgent missions to help them.
Faith: hospitality, preservation of names, mutual aid, and safe passage remain sacred even when institutions fail.
Goal: identify officials who supplied false pilgrims with authentic seals, phrases, and sanctuary customs.
Goal: find Maelis Thorn and determine her involvement.
Fear: her public journey litany supplied information used in the House of Shared Bread attack.
Fear: Maelis knowingly used Bard 1's voice to authenticate a betrayal.
Flaw: places excessive trust in recognized Common Table authority, titles, robes, seals, and appointments.
Habit: records songs phonetically, then separately documents rhythm, breathing, gesture, social setting, and authorized performers.
Habit: scans new settlements for people excluded from normal support and keeps food portions separate for direct charity.
Habit: becomes guarded and formal when a stranger is from a major city.
relationships_and_organizations: The Common Table: Bard 1's religious tradition and active missionary cause; it operates kitchens, guest halls, shrines, road refuges, and networks for food, letters, names, routes, and safe passage.
The House of Shared Bread: former sanctuary and spiritual home; attacked by false pilgrims who stole the Wayfarer Ledger.
The Chorus of Returning Names: independent oral-history network, not formally controlled by the Common Table hierarchy.
Senior Cantor Maelis Thorn: former teacher, institutional sponsor, and unresolved suspect; taught Bard 1 exactness in preserving names and stories.
Mother Orra Vale: wounded during the attack on the House of Shared Bread.
Warlock 1: former fellow acolyte, sanctuary-attack survivor, closest established companion, and original traveling partner; Bard 1 supports her insecurity about appearance and social presence.
Barbarian 1: useful but openly conditional ally whose loyalty depends on perceived benefit.
